about: Steeple Wyke, version 2. The same ten pages as version 1 (../pages.json, ../media/), with each panel's loop files listed in 'loopSrc' (no extension; the page adds .webm or .mp4). Version 1's loops are shared; the bar loops (the scarecrow moved its head and arm) and one minibus loop are left out. 'tiny' marks a short ambient loop made for version 2: about 1.6 s of a clip from the still, played forward and back, so it starts and ends on the still (tools/tiny-loop.sh).

pages.title: The Show
pages.bed: English village summer fete on a field: a large relaxed crowd murmuring and laughing, a distant brass band playing a slow march, children, wind flapping canvas and bunting, skylarks

panels.alt: A village show on a sunny field: a white marquee, bunting, crowds, a brass band, and a church spire behind. Along the hedge, a line of scarecrows.
panels.prompt: Wide establishing shot of an English village horticultural show on a mown field in July: a big white marquee with its side walls rolled up, strings of faded triangle bunting, families with pushchairs, a brass band in maroon jackets on hay bales, trestle tables. Behind the marquee, the honey-coloured stone spire of a village church above trees. Along the hedge at the right, a line of six life-size scarecrows dressed as villagers.
panels.sound: brass band playing a slow march close by, tubas and cornets, a little out of tune, with crowd chatter
loops: Locked-off camera. Bunting flaps gently and the crowd moves slightly. A single gust lifts a white paper plate off a trestle table and sends it rolling across the grass out of frame. Everything else stays still.
Locked-off camera. A small dog on a lead pulls its owner two steps towards the marquee, then sits down. Bunting flaps. Everything else stays still.
Locked-off camera. A child lets go of a red balloon; it rises slowly and drifts out of the top of the frame. The crowd moves slightly.

panels.alt: DCI Quaile at a judging table of chutney jars with a teaspoon; Sam beside her holding a jam jar full of spoons.
panels.prompt: Inside a white show marquee: a trestle table with a white cloth and two rows of home-made chutney jars with handwritten labels and gingham lids. QUAILE stands behind it tasting from a teaspoon with a sceptical face; SAM stands beside her, holding a jam jar full of clean teaspoons, looking patient. Soft daylight through the canvas.
panels.sound: inside a marquee: teaspoons clinking on glass jars, jar lids unscrewing, murmured voices, canvas creaking in the wind

panels.alt: Gerald Pike in a panama hat speaks into a microphone on a stage of hay bales, in front of a table of giant marrows.
panels.prompt: GERALD stands on a low stage of hay bales speaking into an old chrome microphone on a stand, one finger raised. Behind him a table of giant green-striped marrows; the biggest has a red first-prize card. A grey horn loudspeaker is tied to a pole. Bright afternoon sun.
panels.sound: an old public address system: microphone feedback whine, a thump on the microphone, crackle and hum from a horn loudspeaker outdoors

panels.alt: A row of scarecrows along a hedge: a straw vicar in a yellow jacket, a straw butcher in a striped apron, and a straw man in a panama hat facing away.
panels.prompt: A row of handmade scarecrows on posts along a hawthorn hedge at a village show, each dressed as a villager with stuffed sacking faces: one in a bright yellow cycling jacket and a white dog collar, one in a blue-and-white striped butcher's apron with curly red wool hair, one in a cream linen jacket and a panama hat with a red rosette, turned to face the hedge with its back to the camera. Small handwritten entry cards on stakes. Late afternoon sun.
panels.sound: wind moving through dry straw and a hawthorn hedge, a crow cawing twice, a bee passing

pages.title: Behind the produce tent
pages.bed: behind a marquee at an outdoor village show: muffled crowd beyond the canvas, a brass band still playing in the distance, guy ropes creaking, wasps, a woman apologising faintly

Discreet, still, peaceful; no injury, nothing graphic. Long grass, a tent peg, dappled light.
panels.sound: close, quiet outdoor summer air: a fly buzzing near, the canvas of a deckchair creaking, distant crowd

panels.alt: On the grass by the deckchair, a blue enamel flask with a brown luggage label on a string that says Church Hall.

Tied to its handle with string, a brown luggage label handwritten in black marker: CHURCH HALL. Daisies in the grass. Shallow depth of field.
panels.sound: a wasp buzzing close, landing and taking off, grass rustling
loops: Locked-off close-up. A single wasp crawls along the rim of the flask, stops, then flies away out of frame. The grass moves very slightly in the breeze.

Locked-off close-up. A breeze turns the luggage label slowly on its string so its writing faces away, then back again.

SAM stands over her with his black notebook open and a pen. In the deckchair at the edge of frame, only the legs and the cream linen sleeve of a seated man are visible. Afternoon light.

pages.title: Margaret
pages.bed: a quiet English cottage garden in summer: blackbirds and wood pigeons, bees in flowers, a distant tractor, the faint sound of a village show two fields away
